questions.question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

The couple / preferred to walk / until the last house / of the town.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is ‘3’ i.e. until the last house.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase 'until the last house' is incorrect in this context.
 
 
• The correct phrase should be **'up to the last house.'**
 
 
 
• The other segments are grammatically correct.
 
 
• **'The couple'** correctly refers to two people acting together.
 
• **'Preferred to walk'** correctly indicates their choice of activity.
 
• **'Of the town'** correctly indicates the location in question.
 
 

Hence, the correct answer is option 3.

Correct sentence: *The couple preferred to walk up to the last house of the town.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Using 'until' often implies a continuation of action up to a point in time, while 'up to' is more appropriate for physical distances or locations.
 
 
• **Example:** *We walked up to the park entrance.*

questions.question:

questions.solution:

__
 
• The phrase 'violent when' is incorrect in this context.
 
 
• The correct phrase should be **'violently when.'**
 
• This is because 'violently' is the adverb that correctly modifies the verb 'behaving.'
 
 
 
• The other segments are grammatically correct:
 
 
• **'Passengers started behaving'** correctly sets the subject and verb phrase.
 
• **'they were asked'** correctly indicates the action done to the passengers.
 
• **'to leave the bus station'** correctly completes the action that the passengers were asked to do.
 
 

 

Hence, the correct answer is option 2.

Correct sentence: *Passengers started behaving violently when they were asked to leave the bus station.*

questions.question: Select the sentence in the future tense.

options.text: I could be twenty five next Sunday.
I should be twenty five next Sunday.
I have been twenty five next Sunday.
I will be twenty five next Sunday.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is ‘4’ i.e. I will be twenty five next Sunday.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence 'I will be twenty five next Sunday' is in the future tense.
 
 
• The use of **'will be'** indicates an event that is certain to happen in the future.
 
 
 
• The other options are not in the future tense:
 
 
• **Option 1:** 'I could be twenty five next Sunday' uses 'could,' which indicates possibility but not a certain future event.
 
• **Option 2:** 'I should be twenty five next Sunday' uses 'should,' which indicates obligation or expectation, not a certain future event.
 
• **Option 3:** 'I have been twenty five next Sunday' is grammatically incorrect because it mixes present perfect tense with a future time reference.
 
 

 

Hence, the correct answer is option 4.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Future tense in English can be formed using 'will' followed by the base form of the verb.
 
 
• **Example:** *She will arrive tomorrow.*

questions.question: A and B can do a work in 10 days and 40 days, respectively. How long will it take together to complete the work?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A can do a work in 10 days.

B can do the same work in 40 days.

**Formula Used:**

Work done together per day = 1/A + 1/B

Time taken together = 1 / Work done together per day

**Calculation:**

Work done by A in one day = 1/10

Work done by B in one day = 1/40

Work done together per day = 1/10 + 1/40

⇒ Work done together per day = (4 + 1) / 40

⇒ Work done together per day = 5 / 40

⇒ Work done together per day = 1 / 8

Time taken together = 1 / (1/8)

⇒ Time taken together = 8 days

**It will take A and B together 8 days to complete the work.**

questions.question: The ratio of the diameters of two spheres is given as 1 : 4. The larger sphere is melted and 125 identical spheres are made out of the molten material. The smaller sphere is melted and 27 identical spheres are made out of the molten material. If the ratio of the volume of each of the 125 identical spheres to the volume of each of the 27 identical spheres is given as 1 : m, what is the value of m?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Ratio of diameters of two spheres = 1 : 4

Number of identical spheres made from the larger sphere = 125

Number of identical spheres made from the smaller sphere = 27

Ratio of the volume of each of the 125 identical spheres to the volume of each of the 27 identical spheres = 1 : m

**Formula Used:**

Volume of a sphere = (4)/(3)pi r³

Volume ratio of spheres = ((d₁)/(d₂))³ 

**Calculation:**

Let the diameter of the smaller sphere be d. Then the diameter of the larger sphere is 4d.

Let the radius of the smaller sphere be r. Then the radius of the larger sphere is 4r.

Volume of the smaller sphere = (4)/(3)pi r³

Volume of the larger sphere = (4)/(3)pi (4r)³

⇒ Volume of the larger sphere = (4)/(3)pi (64r³)

⇒ Volume of the larger sphere = (256)/(3)pi r³

Volume of each of the 125 identical spheres = (frac{256)/(3)pi r³}{125}

⇒ Volume of each of the 125 identical spheres = (256pi r³)/(375)

Volume of each of the 27 identical spheres = (frac{4)/(3)pi r³}{27}

⇒ Volume of each of the 27 identical spheres = (4pi r³)/(81)

Ratio of the volume of each of the 125 identical spheres to the volume of each of the 27 identical spheres = (frac{256pi r³)/(375)}{(4pi r³)/(81)}

⇒ Ratio = (256pi r³)/(375) times (81)/(4pi r³)

⇒ Ratio = (256 times 81)/(375 times 4)

⇒ Ratio = (20736)/(1500)

⇒ Ratio = 1728/125

⇒ Ratio = 1 : m

⇒ m = (125)/(1728)

**The correct answer is Option 3).**

questions.question: A shopkeeper marks up the price of the oil by 40% and uses a faulty machine which measures 15% less. If the shopkeeper gives a discount of 32%, the profit/loss percentage is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Markup percentage = 40%

Faulty machine measures 15% less

Discount given = 32%

**Formula Used:**

Profit/Loss percentage = (frac{{Selling Price} - {Cost Price}}{{Cost Price}}) times 100 %

**Calculation:**

Let Cost Price (CP) = 100

Marked Price (MP) = 100 + 40% of 100

⇒ MP = 100 + 40

⇒ MP = 140

Due to faulty machine, the quantity measured is 15% less, hence the quantity sold is 85%

⇒ Selling Price (SP) before discount = 140

Discount given = 32% of 140

⇒ Discount = 32% × 140

⇒ Discount = 0.32 × 140

⇒ Discount = 44.8

SP after discount = 140 - 44.8

⇒ SP = 95.2

Effective quantity sold = 85% of CP = 85% of 100

⇒ Effective quantity sold = 85

Profit/Loss = SP - Effective CP

⇒ Profit/Loss = 95.2 - 85

⇒ Profit = 10.2

Profit percentage = ((10.2)/(85)) times 100 %

⇒ Profit percentage = 12%

**The profit percentage is 12%.**

questions.question: If Arun's salary was decreased by 50% and subsequently increased by 50%, then how much per cent did he lose?

Initial salary of Arun = S

Decrease in salary = 50%

Subsequent increase in salary = 50%

**Formula Used:**

Final Salary = Initial Salary × (1 - Decrease%) × (1 + Increase%)

Percentage Loss = ((Initial Salary - Final Salary))/(Initial Salary) times 100

**Calculation:**

Decrease in salary = 50% of S = 0.5S

New salary after decrease = S - 0.5S = 0.5S

Subsequent increase = 50% of 0.5S = 0.25S

Final salary after increase = 0.5S + 0.25S = 0.75S

Percentage Loss = ((S - 0.75S))/(S) times 100

Percentage Loss = (0.25S)/(S) times 100

Percentage Loss = 0.25 × 100

Percentage Loss = 25%

**Arun lost 25% of his salary.**
